# Medical referral review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Typed session coordinator and immutable receipt DTO; an acquired confirmation capability reads native visit identity.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: Compile public Java sources with OpenJDK 11, placing generated classes outside /workspace.
Verify multiple edits within one burst produce no immediate writes and exactly one write of the latest text after 120 ms of quiet.
Verify a later edit burst also saves after its own 120 ms quiet interval.
Verify open, close, submit, and dispose remain synchronous and retain their existing return behavior.
Verify editor lifecycle boundaries cannot allow an older visit's pending callback to overwrite a newer visit's persisted text.
Verify Preview continues to use its existing 40 ms trailing task and hide-cancellation behavior unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue calling env.write directly for every edit.
Do not publish more than one repository write for a single uninterrupted editing burst.
Do not let a pending task owned by an earlier editor visit write into the lifecycle of a later visit.
Do not change the adjacent search preview as part of this maintenance change.
Do not change the synchronous workspace API or the injected store, queue/capture, timer, or output interfaces.
Do not weaken confirmation outlet ownership or allow a receipt to establish an earlier visit identity.
Do not alter tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each call to open creates a fresh Session identity, even when reopening the same document id.
The editor trailing task is owned by the Session created for that visit and must not be treated as workspace-global work.
Confirmation captures the Session active when the capability is acquired and emits only while that exact Session remains current.
A pending callback from a retired Session must not affect a later Session.

obligations.text: Workspace.edit must update the selected Session's in-memory text synchronously, but persistence must be requested through that Session's existing Trailing utility rather than by calling env.write on every edit.
The editor Trailing utility must use a 120 ms delay and, for edits arriving before the quiet interval expires, cancel the prior scheduled handle and retain only the latest text.
After 120 ms without another edit in the burst, exactly one write must persist the latest text for the active editing visit.
After one burst has flushed, later bursts must be independently schedulable and must also persist their latest text.
The change must preserve the synchronous open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and dispose() interfaces, including submit returning the queue receipt or null when no editor is selected.
Opening a document must continue to create a fresh editor visit using persisted repository text, maintain the document-specific store subscription, and render the selected document.
Submission must continue to synchronously capture a snapshot of the selected visit's current in-memory id and text, independently of whether a coalesced repository write is pending.

Retiring or replacing an editor visit must handle its scheduled task so that delayed work from that visit cannot overwrite a later visit; the precise flush-versus-cancel policy at close/open remains an explicit unknown requiring preservation-based resolution.
Preview.query and Preview.hide behavior, including the 40 ms quiet interval and cancellation of unpublished preview work, must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Within an editing burst, updating Session.text occurs synchronously before the delayed persistence callback can observe the value.
Each new edit in a pending burst cancels the previous timer before scheduling the replacement timer.
The normal persistence write occurs only after the final edit has remained quiet for 120 ms.
A completed flush clears its handle and pending value before invoking the write callback, allowing subsequent bursts to schedule normally.
Session retirement must prevent any pending callback from crossing into and corrupting a later visit.
Dispose must detach integrations before the workspace is closed, preserving the documented lifecycle ordering.
preservation: Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores its persisted text.
Store writes continue notifying the existing document-specific subscription and producing status output.
Submission continues using the selected Session's current text and returning the capture receipt synchronously.
The confirmation outlet remains bound to the visit active when it is acquired.
Document and notice clearing behavior on open and close remains supported.
Injected service interfaces and passive output behavior remain unchanged.
Preview timing, cancellation, and later-query usability remain unchanged.
